structures.name: Frontal lobe
structures.tagline: Planning, deciding and moving.

structures.name: Prefrontal cortex
structures.tagline: Keeps goals in mind and puts the brakes on impulses.

structures.name: Primary motor cortex
structures.tagline: Shapes voluntary movement commands sent toward the spinal cord.

structures.name: Broca's area
structures.tagline: Helps plan speech, grammar and demanding language sequences.

structures.name: Parietal lobe
structures.tagline: Touch, body sense and where things are in space.

structures.name: Primary somatosensory cortex
structures.tagline: Where touch, temperature and pain from your body arrive.

structures.name: Posterior parietal cortex
structures.tagline: Builds a map of space so you can reach and look.

structures.name: Temporal lobe
structures.tagline: Hearing, language and recognising what things are.

structures.name: Primary auditory cortex
structures.tagline: The first stop in the cortex for sound.

structures.name: Wernicke's area
structures.tagline: Helps you understand the words you hear and read.

structures.name: Occipital lobe
structures.tagline: The vision department at the back of your head.

structures.name: Primary visual cortex
structures.tagline: Breaks what you see into edges, lines and motion.

structures.name: Cingulate cortex
structures.tagline: Notices mistakes and conflict, and links feelings to action.

structures.name: Insula
structures.tagline: Your sense of the inside of your body: heartbeat, hunger, disgust.

structures.name: Thalamus
structures.tagline: The relay station that passes almost every sense on to the cortex.

structures.name: Hypothalamus
structures.tagline: Runs the body: hunger, thirst, temperature, sleep and hormones.

structures.name: Striatum
structures.tagline: Learns habits and helps pick which action to do next.

structures.name: Globus pallidus
structures.tagline: The brake pedal on movement, released only for the right action.

structures.name: Substantia nigra
structures.tagline: Uses dopamine and inhibitory output to tune movement circuits.

structures.name: Hippocampus
structures.tagline: Turns what happened today into memories you can recall later.

structures.name: Amygdala
structures.tagline: The alarm that flags danger and gives memories emotional weight.

structures.name: Corpus callosum
structures.tagline: A thick cable of fibres that lets the two halves talk.

structures.name: Ventral tegmental area
structures.tagline: Sends learning and motivation signals through several dopamine pathways.

structures.name: Basal forebrain
structures.tagline: Sends acetylcholine widely to tune attention, learning and wakefulness.

structures.name: Nucleus accumbens
structures.tagline: Ventral striatum that translates reward signals and motivation into action.

structures.name: Pituitary gland
structures.tagline: The master endocrine gland that releases hormones into the bloodstream.

structures.name: Pineal gland
structures.tagline: Produces melatonin in the dark to set your daily sleep and wake rhythm.

structures.name: Mammillary bodies
structures.tagline: Relays memory signals from the hippocampus to the thalamus.

structures.name: Habenula
structures.tagline: Signals disappointment and brakes dopamine when an expected reward fails.

structures.name: Olfactory bulb
structures.tagline: The sensory station for smell, wired directly to memory and emotion.

structures.name: Cerebellum
structures.tagline: Fine-tunes movement so it comes out smooth, timed and accurate.

structures.name: Midbrain
structures.tagline: Reflex hub for eyes and ears, and home of the dopamine cells.

structures.name: Pons
structures.tagline: A bridge carrying signals between the cortex and the cerebellum.

structures.name: Medulla oblongata
structures.tagline: Keeps you alive on autopilot: breathing, heart rate, swallowing.

structures.name: Spinal cord
structures.tagline: The main cable between brain and body.

structures.name: Raphe nuclei
structures.tagline: Brainstem nuclei that send serotonin through widespread circuits.

structures.name: Locus coeruleus
structures.tagline: A small noradrenaline system that retunes alertness and attention.

chemicals.name: Glutamate
chemicals.tagline: The main go signal of the brain, driving fast thoughts and helping build memories.

chemicals.name: GABA
chemicals.tagline: The main calming messenger of the brain, keeping neural activity balanced and under control.

chemicals.name: Dopamine
chemicals.tagline: Signals reward surprises, tunes voluntary movement, and shapes motivation.

chemicals.name: Serotonin
chemicals.tagline: Broadcasts from the brainstem to steady mood, patience, appetite, sleep, and pain.

chemicals.name: Noradrenaline
chemicals.tagline: Snaps the brain to high alert, sharpens attention, and primes the body for action.

chemicals.name: Acetylcholine
chemicals.tagline: Commands muscle contraction, sharpens attention, and helps encode new memories.

chemicals.name: Cortisol
chemicals.tagline: Mobilises energy, sharpens alertness under stress, and quiets inflammation.

chemicals.name: Adrenaline
chemicals.tagline: Triggers the rapid fight-or-flight surge, accelerating heart rate and opening airways.

chemicals.name: Oxytocin
chemicals.tagline: Promotes social bonding, maternal care, and physical birth contractions.

chemicals.name: Vasopressin
chemicals.tagline: Conserves body water, concentrates urine, and raises blood pressure.

chemicals.name: Melatonin
chemicals.tagline: Signals environmental darkness to coordinate the biological sleep clock.

chemicals.name: Thyroid hormone
chemicals.tagline: Sets the metabolic burn rate of every cell, governing warmth and energy.

chemicals.name: Leptin
chemicals.tagline: Signals body fat reserves to the brain, curbing appetite and approving reproduction.

chemicals.name: Ghrelin
chemicals.tagline: The hunger hormone released by an empty stomach to drive food seeking.

chemicals.name: Growth hormone
chemicals.tagline: Stimulates tissue growth, bone lengthening, muscle protein synthesis, and cellular repair.

chemicals.name: Sex hormones
chemicals.tagline: Drives sexual maturation, reproductive cycles, bone strength, and social behaviour.

chemicals.name: Prolactin
chemicals.tagline: Promotes milk production after birth and fosters nurturing parental instincts.
